chunks: And from him, from Ahmad, from Al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If his doubt is established regarding the third and the fourth, he should conclude (the prayer), and pray two rak'at, and four prostrations with the Opening of the Book while he is seated, intending in the Tashahhud.
ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for prayer when one doubts whether they have prayed three or four rak'at?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the procedure for *sahw* (forgetfulness) when a worshipper doubts whether they have completed three or four rak'at, a common scenario in Shia jurisprudence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs the individual to conclude the prayer, then perform two additional rak'at while seated, culminating in four prostrations reciting only Surah Al-Fatiha. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on resolving doubt through specific compensatory acts rather than restarting the prayer, ensuring the validity of the worship despite uncertainty.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad, from Al Husayn, from Fazalat, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If his imagination is established regarding the third and the fourth, he should greet (complete the Salāt), and he should pray two Rak’at of Salāt, and four Sajdah with the Opening of the Book while he is seated, intending in the Tashahhud’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by Ahmad ibn al-Husayn from Fadalah from al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If one’s guess settles on his performing three or four Rak‘at, he says the phrase of offering greeting of peace, then performs two Rak‘at and four Sujud (prostrations) with al-Fatihah al-Kitab in a sitting position and says Tashahhud (testimonies of belief).”’
